audit.whatIsWrong: The mid text says 'she has no dash, so a well-placed Miasma locks her dashless feet in place' and the late text calls her 'immobile with no escape'. Both are false, and the full layer calls Illaoi 'he' in the TL;DR, win condition, three phase whys, both trade lines, the snowball line and a trigger card.
audit.why: Harsh Lesson is a dash: 'Illaoi leaps to her target, dealing physical damage and causing nearby Tentacles to also swing at the target', on a flat 4s cooldown. Selling Miasma as a lock on an immobile champion is the wrong reason for the right play — Miasma matters precisely BECAUSE she has a leap, since grounding stops movement abilities.
audit.corrected: Harsh Lesson named as a 4s leap in both layers, the grounding sold as the answer to that leap, and the pronouns fixed to her.

audit.whatIsWrong: Test of Spirit is called the clock on six lines with no number, and Harsh Lesson, Tentacle Smash and Leap of Faith are never given cooldowns at all.
audit.why: Test of Spirit is 16/15/14/13/12s, Harsh Lesson a flat 4s, Tentacle Smash 10/9/8/7/6s and Leap of Faith 120/95/70s, against your Miasma at 24s. A 4s leap versus a 24s grounding is why you ground the fight location rather than the engage.
audit.corrected: 16s, 4s, 10s, 120s and your own 24s written into the cooldown block, the trigger card, the win condition and the wants list.

audit.whatIsWrong: Nothing anywhere warns you not to damage your own spirit, even though your Q is an area blast and your W is a cloud, and the page tells you to keep poking after a Test of Spirit lands.
audit.why: Riot's Test of Spirit text: 'Spirits echo a percentage of the damage they take to the original target.' You are the original target, so any Noxious Blast or Miasma tick that clips your own spirit comes straight back onto your health bar. Separately Prophet of an Elder God spawns tentacles 'on nearby impassible terrain' and heals her off them, so wall-hugging builds her field for her and Grievous Wounds matters in any long fight.
audit.corrected: The self-echo rule written into the 3-5 spike, the treadmill phase and the key-interactions slot; fighting away from walls tied to the terrain-spawn rule.

The rule that never changes: kill her on open ground away from walls, since her tentacles spawn on impassible terrain. Stand in the field and her sustain wins; pull her out with W and she is a slow target I delete.

notes: Illaoi's Leap of Faith carries derived 'grounding' and 'untargetable' flags in the kit file, but Riot's own description says only that she smashes her idol, damages nearby enemies and spawns a tentacle per champion hit — no untargetability and no grounding. Per the trust-the-description rule I ignored the untargetable-dodges-burst entry in _missing-interactions.json and wrote nothing suggesting you should wait out an untargetable window. Grievous Wounds is warranted against the Prophet of an Elder God tentacle healing. Twin Fang's derived 'projectile' flag contradicts its targeted description and nothing here relies on it.
